key_insight: This paper introduces "Sustainability Robotics" as a unifying discipline that connects robotics research with sustainability goals. It proposes a shared framework to reduce fragmentation and improve both environmental and societal impact.
problem_solved: Robotics research is currently fragmented across many applications and lacks a cohesive sustainability-oriented direction. The paper addresses the need for a framework that guides robotics toward measurable benefits for people and the planet.
method: Defines Sustainability Robotics as a new discipline with a clear mission and scope.
Introduces three guiding principles to steer research and development.
Organizes the field across two dimensions: sustainable design and robotics for sustainability.
impact: For AI/ML and robotics practitioners, this provides a strategic lens for designing systems that are not only technically effective but also socially responsible and environmentally beneficial. It can help align research agendas, evaluation criteria, and deployment decisions with sustainability outcomes.
visual_elements: A two-axis framework diagram showing sustainable design vs. robotics for sustainability
Three-icon panel illustrating the guiding principles
A flowchart connecting fragmented robotics research to sustainability impact
An ecosystem graphic showing benefits to environment, society, and technology
paper_authors: S. Song, B. Mazzolai, M. Kovač
